title: Different Screens
evidence_boundary: Established: aphantasia, hyperphantasia, and inner-speech variation are documented. The screen, interface, graphics-settings, and factory-setting language is metaphor.
grounding: The closing beats return the viewer to their own room and breath.
invitation: Compare inner experience with curiosity rather than assuming one standard mind.
end_card_question: What else might become worth asking?
voice_standard: Liam - warm, sly, a brilliant friend at midnight; spacious and intimate through the turn, near-whisper on the closing question.

scenes.text: Close your eyes and picture a red apple. Make it glossy. Slowly turn it beneath a kitchen light.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The viewer deliberately pictures a glossy red apple.
scenes.primary_symbol: A real glossy red apple rotates slowly on a small turntable
scenes.query: A real glossy red apple rotates slowly on a small turntable beneath a warm kitchen pendant light; rich red accent, moving reflections, landscape framing with clean title space.

scenes.text: Can you actually see it, almost like a photograph floating somewhere behind your eyelids?
scenes.semantic_anchor: Mental imagery can feel photographically visible behind closed eyes.
scenes.primary_symbol: A person closes their eyes while holding a red apple; shallo
scenes.query: A person closes their eyes while holding a red apple; shallow focus shifts from the moving apple to the closed eyelids under soft window light.

scenes.text: Or did you receive only the idea of apple—no color, no shape, no tiny grocery-store commercial?
scenes.semantic_anchor: Some imagination supplies only the concept rather than a vivid image.
scenes.primary_symbol: An artist studies a real apple and actively sketches only a
scenes.query: An artist studies a real apple and actively sketches only a faint graphite outline, leaving the page uncolored as the pencil moves.

scenes.text: Some people see absolutely nothing, while still knowing exactly what an apple is.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Conceptual knowledge can remain when visual imagery is absent.
scenes.primary_symbol: With eyes closed, a person confidently reaches into a fruit
scenes.query: With eyes closed, a person confidently reaches into a fruit bowl and lifts the correct apple; frame stays on the moving hand and fruit.

scenes.text: Established science: this spectrum includes aphantasia and hyperphantasia. Human imagination does not ship with one standard display.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Established imagery vividness varies from aphantasia to hyperphantasia.
scenes.primary_symbol: A tracking camera passes a wall of active monitors showing t
scenes.query: A tracking camera passes a wall of active monitors showing the same rotating apple from blank black, to faint outline, to vivid photographic detail.

scenes.text: Apparently, consciousness arrived with different graphics settings, and reality forgot to include the instruction manual.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Different minds operate with different internal display settings.
scenes.primary_symbol: A hand adjusts brightness, resolution, and detail sliders on
scenes.query: A hand adjusts brightness, resolution, and detail sliders on a real display while a rotating apple visibly changes clarity; camera remains locked and readable.
scenes.symbol_query: slowly rotating globe reflected against moving city streets in clear daylight

scenes.text: You may have spent your entire life assuming everyone was watching the same internal screen.
scenes.semantic_anchor: People assume others share their private inner display.
scenes.primary_symbol: A moving train passes commuters absorbed in differently colo
scenes.query: A moving train passes commuters absorbed in differently colored screens, each display reflecting a distinct image across the carriage windows.

scenes.text: They are not.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Internal experience is not identical across people.
scenes.primary_symbol: Two adjacent monitors play unmistakably different moving ver
scenes.query: Two adjacent monitors play unmistakably different moving versions of the same red apple as focus snaps decisively from one screen to the other.

scenes.text: Some minds render in cinematic detail. Some produce a sketch. Others simply display the file name: APPLE.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Minds can represent one concept as imagery, sketchlike imagery, or nonvisual knowledge.
scenes.primary_symbol: Three adjacent workstations show the same apple as a moving
scenes.query: Three adjacent workstations show the same apple as a moving photoreal 3D model, an actively drawn pencil sketch, and a file browser labeled APPLE.
scenes.symbol_query: hand moves magnifying glass across printed words on paper natural side light close up

scenes.text: Established science: inner speech varies too. Some people hear a narrator commenting on nearly everything.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Established inner speech can accompany much of daily activity.
scenes.primary_symbol: A podcast microphone and live waveform remain active while a
scenes.query: A podcast microphone and live waveform remain active while a person makes coffee and organizes a kitchen, suggesting continuous commentary during ordinary action.

scenes.text: Others think without any voice inside their head. No internal podcast reviewing every sandwich.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Thought can organize action without an internal verbal narrator.
scenes.primary_symbol: A quiet craftsperson assembles a wooden geometric puzzle bes
scenes.query: A quiet craftsperson assembles a wooden geometric puzzle beside an untouched microphone, guided by precise hand and object movement.

scenes.text: Neither mind is empty. Neither is more conscious. They use different interfaces to organize experience.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Different cognitive interfaces can both support full conscious experience.
scenes.primary_symbol: Two distinct control panels route moving signals by differen
scenes.query: Two distinct control panels route moving signals by different paths to produce the same completed apple image on paired output screens.

scenes.text: That means arguments can involve two people comparing conclusions from screens neither person can inspect.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Arguments compare conclusions drawn from inaccessible private experience.
scenes.primary_symbol: Two people stand on opposite sides of a translucent divider,
scenes.query: Two people stand on opposite sides of a translucent divider, each pointing to a different moving diagram that the other person cannot see.

scenes.text: You say, “Obviously.” They say, “Obviously.” Reality waits backstage, wondering which version of obvious you ordered.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Conflicting private experiences can both feel self-evident.
scenes.primary_symbol: On a theater stage, two illuminated OBVIOUS signs point in o
scenes.query: On a theater stage, two illuminated OBVIOUS signs point in opposite directions while moving backstage rigging switches attention between them; stabilized camera.

scenes.text: This does not mean evidence stops mattering. The outside world still pushes back against our private models.
scenes.semantic_anchor: External evidence constrains private interpretations.
scenes.primary_symbol: A hand load-tests a small model bridge; the structure bends
scenes.query: A hand load-tests a small model bridge; the structure bends under real weight while a measuring gauge moves and records the response.

scenes.text: It means your rendering is not humanity’s factory setting. It is one configuration among billions.
scenes.semantic_anchor: One person's inner rendering is one configuration among many.
scenes.primary_symbol: A vast factory conveyor carries many differently configured
scenes.query: A vast factory conveyor carries many differently configured active screens, each displaying its own moving interpretation of a red apple.

scenes.text: And that realization can loosen something.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Recognizing cognitive difference loosens rigid assumptions.
scenes.primary_symbol: A tightly knotted cable harness gradually loosens as moving
scenes.query: A tightly knotted cable harness gradually loosens as moving strands separate into clean independent pathways under warm practical light.

scenes.text: Maybe someone who “doesn’t get it” is not refusing your picture. Maybe no picture appeared.
scenes.semantic_anchor: A person may lack the expected mental picture rather than resist it.
scenes.primary_symbol: A working projector beams toward a wall but its image frame
scenes.query: A working projector beams toward a wall but its image frame remains empty while a person calmly checks the lens and waits beside it.

scenes.text: Maybe their silence is not emptiness. Their mind may work somewhere your interface cannot display.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Invisible mental processing is not absence of thought.
scenes.primary_symbol: Inside a live data center, pulses of light travel through hi
scenes.query: Inside a live data center, pulses of light travel through hidden cable routes behind a dark display while cooling fans and indicators keep moving.

scenes.text: Now come back to the room.
scenes.semantic_anchor: The viewer returns from abstraction to their immediate room.
scenes.primary_symbol: A wide, ordinary sunlit room breathes with moving curtains a
scenes.query: A wide, ordinary sunlit room breathes with moving curtains and shifting daylight around an empty chair; slow live camera glide.

scenes.text: Feel your body touching the chair. Watch light move across an object. Listen for the farthest sound.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Body contact, moving light, and distant sound ground perception in the present.
scenes.primary_symbol: A seated person presses both feet into the floor as sunlight
scenes.query: A seated person presses both feet into the floor as sunlight travels across a nearby mug and distant curtains flutter in the same readable room.

scenes.text: This ordinary moment is assembled uniquely inside you, yet we still find ways to meet.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Unique inner experiences can still meet in shared life.
scenes.primary_symbol: Different apartment windows illuminate one by one before nei
scenes.query: Different apartment windows illuminate one by one before neighbors enter a shared hallway and greet each other in warm evening light.

scenes.text: Later, ask someone to picture an apple. Don’t ask whether they did it correctly. Ask what actually appeared.
scenes.semantic_anchor: Curiosity compares subjective imagery without judging it.
scenes.primary_symbol: Two friends at a kitchen table close their eyes, then separa
scenes.query: Two friends at a kitchen table close their eyes, then separately draw what they imagined and turn over two visibly different apple pictures.

scenes.text: And if their screen surprises you, what else might become worth asking?
scenes.semantic_anchor: Surprise about one inner difference opens curiosity about many others.
scenes.primary_symbol: Many real apple drawings from different people unfold across
scenes.query: Many real apple drawings from different people unfold across a table as hands point, compare, and respond with visible curiosity; closing visual reframes the entire premise.
